name: Evolocumab
route_note: subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks or once monthly (prefilled pen or on-body infusor)

discovery.note: A fully human IgG2 antibody developed after genetics linked PCSK9 to LDL cholesterol levels. Year is the priority date of the Amgen PCSK9 antigen-binding protein patent (US 8,030,457).

tagline: Fully human anti-PCSK9 antibody that lowers LDL by about 60%
summary: Evolocumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody that binds PCSK9 and prevents it from degrading LDL receptors. Given by subcutaneous injection, it lowers LDL cholesterol by roughly 60% on top of statins, and the FOURIER trial showed fewer cardiovascular events.
mechanism: PCSK9 is a liver-secreted protein that binds LDL receptors on hepatocytes and directs them to lysosomes for destruction instead of recycling to the cell surface.
Evolocumab binds circulating PCSK9 and blocks its interaction with the LDL receptor, so more receptors recycle and clear LDL from the blood. It also lowers lipoprotein(a) by about 25–30%.
uses: Reduction of myocardial infarction, stroke and coronary revascularisation in established cardiovascular disease
Primary hyperlipidaemia including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (adults and children ≥10)

history.title: PCSK9 genetics
history.detail: Gain-of-function PCSK9 mutations are found to cause familial hypercholesterolaemia.

history.title: Loss-of-function protection
history.detail: People with PCSK9 loss-of-function variants are shown to have low LDL and fewer coronary events.

history.title: Approvals
history.detail: Approved in the EU (July) and the US (August).

history.title: FOURIER
history.detail: Evolocumab reduces major cardiovascular events by 15% in patients with atherosclerotic disease.

history.title: Price cut
history.detail: Amgen cuts the US list price by about 60% to improve access.

history.title: Paediatric use
history.detail: FDA approves use in children with familial hypercholesterolaemia.

pk.metabolism: Saturable target-mediated binding to PCSK9 and non-specific proteolysis
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody

facts: FOURIER found no excess of cognitive adverse events at very low LDL levels, and the EBBINGHAUS sub-study supported this.

references.title: Sabatine MS et al. Evolocumab and clinical outcomes in patients with cardiovascular disease (FOURIER). N Engl J Med 2017
